import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 1

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture1

open SimpleGraph

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 1](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G` the maximum number of leaves of a spanning
tree satisfies `Ls(G) ≥ n(G) + 1 - 2·m(G)` where `n(G)` counts vertices and
`m(G)` is the size of a maximum matching.

A formal proof reduces to a spanning tree `T`. If `I` is the set of non-leaves
of `T`, Hall's theorem applied to a bipartition of `T` gives a matching `M`
with `|I| + 1 ≤ 2 * |M|`. Since `|V|` is the sum of the numbers of leaves and
non-leaves, and every matching and leaf count constructed in `T` is admissible
for the corresponding supremum in `G`, the stated inequality follows.
-/

@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/MiskinAleksandr23/WOWII-1/blob/eda16f6e96b313bd112351ae9859133b77d537c9/WOWII1/GraphConjecture1.lean"]
theorem conjecture1 {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    (Fintype.card α : ℝ) + 1 - 2 * matchingNumber G ≤ (Ls G : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture1

findings.description: The docstring at lines 33–35 states the bound for a simple connected graph without mentioning the necessary restriction to at least two vertices. The Lean theorem correctly imposes `[Nontrivial α]`. For the connected one-vertex graph, both `matchingNumber` and `Ls` are 0, so the unrestricted prose assertion would require 2 ≤ 0. This is only a docstring omission; the theorem itself matches the source.
findings.source_evidence: The remarks immediately following WOWII Conjecture 1 explicitly say that Fajtlowicz proved the inequality for “connected graphs on at least two vertices,” and reiterate “for graphs with at least one edge.” Read at https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161837id_/http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html .
findings.suggested_fix: Begin the docstring: “For a finite simple connected graph G with at least two vertices, the maximum number of leaves of a spanning tree satisfies …”. No change to the Lean statement is needed.

reformulations.difference: The source uses maximum combinatorial counts, whereas `matchingNumber` and `Ls` are implemented as suprema of sets of real-valued cardinalities.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite graph has finitely many subgraphs. The matching collection is nonempty because it contains the empty matching; the spanning-tree collection is nonempty because G is connected. Thus both real suprema are attained maxima. Matching subgraphs represent vertex-disjoint edges, and spanning-tree leaves are precisely the vertices of degree one in the tree, as defined by the source. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, `Review.real_inequality_iff_finite_maxima` proves that the Lean inequality is equivalent to the existence of natural-valued maxima m and l satisfying |V| + 1 ≤ l + 2*m.

review.notes: No theorem-level misformalization or status mismatch was found. The source marks Conjecture 1 true and credits Fajtlowicz (1996), agreeing with `research solved`. The cited external proof has the identical statement; after three API-only compatibility edits in the scratch copy, its dependency and theorem compile, and `#print axioms` reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Independent scratch checks establish matchingNumber(K₂)=1 and Ls(K₂)=2, verify the inequality for K₂, and refute its unrestricted singleton version. All experiments are under /workspace/review/.
